import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Dataset not found. Please ensure 'data/dogs_zurich.csv' is in the correct directory.")
    exit()

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Filter for the most recent year's data to get a current snapshot
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year].copy()

# Drop rows with missing age or breed information
df_latest.dropna(subset=['AlterVHundNum', 'Rasse1Text'], inplace=True)

# Clean and shorten breed names for better readability on the plot
breed_name_mapping = {
    'Mischling klein (< 45 cm)': 'Small Mixed-Breed (<45cm)',
    'Mischling mittel (45-60 cm)': 'Medium Mixed-Breed (45-60cm)',
    'Franz. Bulldogge': 'French Bulldog',
    'Jack Russel Terrier': 'Jack Russell Terrier',
    'Mischling gross (> 60 cm)': 'Large Mixed-Breed (>60cm)'
}
df_latest['Rasse1Text'] = df_latest['Rasse1Text'].replace(breed_name_mapping)

# Identify the top 12 most popular breeds
top_breeds_series = df_latest['Rasse1Text'].value_counts()
N_BREEDS = 12
top_breeds = top_breeds_series.nlargest(N_BREEDS).index

# Filter the dataframe to include only the top breeds
df_top_breeds = df_latest[df_latest['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_breeds)]

# Calculate median age for sorting the breeds on the plot
median_ages = df_top_breeds.groupby('Rasse1Text')['AlterVHundNum'].median().sort_values(ascending=False)
sorted_breeds_by_age = median_ages.index

# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 10))

# Create the boxplot, ordering breeds by median age
sns.boxplot(
    data=df_top_breeds,
    y='Rasse1Text',
    x='AlterVHundNum',
    order=sorted_breeds_by_age,
    palette='viridis_r',
    ax=ax,
    fliersize=2,
    linewidth=1.2
)

# Add individual data points with jitter for better distribution visibility
sns.stripplot(
    data=df_top_breeds,
    y='Rasse1Text',
    x='AlterVHundNum',
    order=sorted_breeds_by_age,
    ax=ax,
    size=2,
    color='black',
    alpha=0.1
)

# --- Annotations and Styling ---

# Set title and labels with descriptive text
fig.suptitle(
    f'Age Distribution of Popular Dog Breeds in Zurich ({latest_year})',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    y=0.96
)
ax.set_title(
    f'Comparison of the {N_BREEDS} most common breeds, sorted by median age. Each point represents one dog.',
    fontsize=14,
    pad=10,
    color='dimgray'
)
ax.set_xlabel('Dog Age (Years)', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Breed', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)

# Customize ticks and grid
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(2))
ax.xaxis.grid(True, linestyle='--', which='major', color='grey', alpha=0.5)
ax.yaxis.grid(False)

# Add annotations for median age on each boxplot
for i, breed in enumerate(sorted_breeds_by_age):
    median_val = median_ages[breed]
    ax.text(
        median_val,
        i,
        f' {median_val:.1f}',
        va='center',
        ha='left',
        fontsize=11,
        color='white',
        fontweight='bold',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.2", fc='black', ec='none', alpha=0.6)
    )

# Despine for a cleaner look
sns.despine(trim=True, left=True)

# --- Save the Figure ---
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
